Digital payments have made routine banking faster and more accessible. Customers can transfer money, pay bills and check
balances without visiting a branch. Yet the convenience of digital banking does not remove the need for caution. Users should verify
payment details, avoid sharing one-time passwords and report suspicious activity promptly. Banks also invest in authentication,
transaction monitoring and customer awareness to reduce fraud. Thus, technology can improve banking efficiency, but secure habits
remain essential.

Digital payments have made routine banking faster and more accessible. Customers can transfer money, pay bills and check
balances without visiting a branch. Yet the convenience of digital banking does not remove the need for caution. Users should verify
payment details, avoid sharing one-time passwords and report suspicious activity promptly. Banks also invest in authentication,
transaction monitoring and customer awareness to reduce fraud. Thus, technology can improve banking efficiency, but secure habits
remain essential.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
questions.context:
Directions (Q1–5): Read the passage and answer the questions.
The growth of digital payments has changed the way customers interact with banks. Transactions that once required a visit to a branch can now often be completed within minutes. Yet convenience must be accompanied by awareness. Customers should verify beneficiaries, protect authentication details and review transaction alerts. Banks, meanwhile, need to maintain reliable systems and respond quickly when suspicious activity is reported. The effectiveness of digital banking therefore depends on both technology and responsible usage.

Digital banking needs both reliable technology and responsible customer behaviour.
Customers should stop using payment apps.
questions.correctAnswer: Digital banking needs both reliable technology and responsible customer behaviour.

questions.question: What can strengthen a savings habit?
questions.context:
Directions (Q6–10): Read the passage and answer the questions.
A savings habit can be strengthened when people set a clear target and monitor progress regularly. A person who saves a fixed amount every month may gradually build an emergency fund without making a large one-time sacrifice. However, saving is only one part of financial planning. Individuals should also distinguish between essential and discretionary spending, understand the cost of borrowing and keep adequate records. A simple and consistent process can make financial decisions more deliberate.
